Bill number: HB1498
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1487
 By Powers

 HOUSE BILL 1498

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of safety,

 health, or behavioral issues exhibited by a student and includes, but is not limited to,

 indicators of a student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation,

 bullying, or cyberbullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of

 substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the harassment, intimidation, bullying, and cyberbullying

 policy adopted by the LEA in accordance with § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline

 Act, compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and with each school safety plan adopted

 by the LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA personnel serving on the LEA's threat

 assessment team created pursuant to § 49-6-2701, or the employee of the public

 charter school who is designated to receive such notification, when an early

 warning sign is entered into the system for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

notification, as well as any other notifications previously received for the student, and

determine whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior.

 (f)

 (1) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to

 the department of education that provides the following data collected by the LEA

 or public charter school in the immediately preceding school year:

 (A) The number of early warning signs input into the system;

 (B) The number of early warning signs input into the system,

 disaggregated by the number input by a:

 (i) Teacher, disaggregated further by the grade levels and

 subject areas taught by such teachers; and

 (ii) School staff, disaggregated further by the position,

 assignment, and duties of such school staff;

 (C)

 (i) The number of students for whom more than one (1)

 early warning sign was input into the system; and

 (ii) The number of early warning signs for each student for

 whom more than one (1) early warning sign input into the system;

 (D) A general description of the types of early warning signs input

 into the system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified; and

 (E) A general description of the actions taken by the LEA or

 public charter school in response to each early warning sign input into the

 system; provided, that a description must not include details or

 information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (2) Reports provided pursuant to this subsection (f) must not include any

 details or information that would allow a student to be identified.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 (i) Subsections (c)-(e) do not apply to an LEA or public charter school that

maintains a system for documenting early warning signs demonstrated by students that

was implemented in the LEA or public charter school before July 1, 2026; provided, that

the LEA or public charter school continuously maintains and utilizes the system.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would require Tennessee local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to use a computer-based system to record students’ early warning signs. These signs include evidence of safety, health, or behavior concerns, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts. Teachers and school staff would have to enter the information, and LEAs and charter schools would have to train them to recognize signs and use the system.

The system would have to align with specified bullying, discipline, and school safety policies. It would have to store the entries and immediately notify the LEA’s threat assessment team personnel or a designated charter school employee. The person notified would review the entry and any earlier entries for that student and decide whether further action is needed. These system, training, and review requirements would not apply to an LEA or charter school that implemented a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026, if it continues to maintain and use that system.

Each LEA and charter school would have to report annually to the education department on the preceding school year. The report would include counts of warning signs, breakdowns by the teachers or staff who entered them, counts for students with multiple entries, and general descriptions of the signs and responses. Reports could not identify students and would have to comply with applicable privacy laws. If an LEA or charter school did not comply, the education commissioner could withhold an amount of state funding the commissioner determines until it complies. The bill would take effect July 1, 2026.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: These signs include evidence of safety, health, or behavior concerns, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the broad definition and several examples, but omits harassment, intimidation, and cyberbullying and does not expressly cover both engaging in and experiencing misconduct or making and receiving threats.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would require Tennessee local education agencies (LEAs) and public charter schools to use a computer-based system to record students’ early warning signs. These signs include evidence of safety, health, or behavior concerns, such as bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal thoughts. Teachers and school staff would have to enter the information, and LEAs and charter schools would have to train them to recognize signs and use the system.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the schools' system obligation and mandatory teacher and staff entry of student warning signs. The summary separately states the existing-system exemption.

assessments.summary_quote: Teachers and school staff would have to enter the information, and LEAs and charter schools would have to train them to recognize signs and use the system.
assessments.rationale: Covers training teachers and staff in identifying signs and using the system, with the exemption explained later.

assessments.summary_quote: The system would have to align with specified bullying, discipline, and school safety policies.
assessments.rationale: Conveys alignment in all three subject areas, but substitutes generic policies for the School Discipline Act and each adopted school safety plan and does not convey the full scope of the harassment-related policy.

assessments.summary_quote: It would have to store the entries
assessments.rationale: In context, storing the required teacher and staff entries conveys the database's receiving and maintaining function without needing the technical term.

assessments.summary_quote: It would have to store the entries and immediately notify the LEA’s threat assessment team personnel or a designated charter school employee.
assessments.rationale: Conveys immediate entry-triggered notification and the correct recipients.

assessments.summary_quote: The person notified would review the entry and any earlier entries for that student and decide whether further action is needed.
assessments.rationale: Conveys review of the current and previous notifications and the decision on further action. The following sentence supplies the exemption.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA and charter school would have to report annually to the education department on the preceding school year. The report would include counts of warning signs
assessments.rationale: Identifies the reporting entities, recipient, annual frequency, preceding-school-year period, and warning-sign count.

assessments.summary_quote: breakdowns by the teachers or staff who entered them
assessments.rationale: Conveys breakdowns by entry source, but omits teacher grade levels and subject areas and staff position, assignment, and duties.

assessments.summary_quote: counts for students with multiple entries
assessments.rationale: Recognizes reporting on students with multiple entries, but does not clearly require both the number of such students and the number of signs for each student.

assessments.summary_quote: general descriptions of the signs and responses. Reports could not identify students
assessments.rationale: Conveys general descriptions and the identification prohibition, but does not specify that the school's response to each entered sign must be described.
Conveys the prohibition on identifying information throughout the annual reports.

assessments.summary_quote: Reports could not identify students and would have to comply with applicable privacy laws.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the comprehensive privacy-law compliance requirement; the individual statutory names and citations are not essential to this description.

assessments.summary_quote: If an LEA or charter school did not comply, the education commissioner could withhold an amount of state funding the commissioner determines until it complies.
assessments.rationale: Conveys noncompliance as the condition, the commissioner's discretion over withholding and amount, and compliance as the endpoint.

assessments.summary_quote: These system, training, and review requirements would not apply to an LEA or charter school that implemented a system for documenting early warning signs before July 1, 2026, if it continues to maintain and use that system.
assessments.rationale: States the exempted requirements, qualifying system, cutoff date, and continued maintenance and use condition. The subsequent reporting requirement expressly applies to each LEA and charter school.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would take effect July 1, 2026.
